sources.finding: FS append-only attribute permits write opens only in append mode; set/clear requires superuser or CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE.
FS_APPEND_FL restricts opens to O_APPEND even for superuser; changing flag requires CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE.
RWF_NOAPPEND exists since Linux 6.9 and can ignore O_APPEND for pwritev2; O_APPEND alone is not a future-proof confinement boundary.
Landlock controls file/open/truncate rights but is inode/path-hierarchy oriented and does not create byte-range write isolation; already-open FDs have important semantics.
verity files are read-only; this strongly protects immutable whole files but conflicts with a same-inode mutable tail.
loop devices can expose a backing file at an offset with a size limit, forming a conventional kernel subrange-view alternative.
Append-only Merkle logs and consistency proofs are established prior art; MOLT cannot claim novelty for append-only cryptographic history.
Immutable databases with cryptographically linked append history are established; generic immutable/append-only DB semantics are prior art.

sources.finding: Executable plus appended mutable KV store is known; physical self-contained executable persistence is not novel by itself.

destructive_findings: O_APPEND alone rejected as security boundary because newer Linux exposes RWF_NOAPPEND.
Hash-chain/append-only history novelty collapses to known analogues.
fs-verity cannot directly protect only an immutable prefix of a writable same file.
Split layout remains the strongest simplicity/least-privilege control.
surviving_transfer: Combine kernel inode append-only enforcement + no-write-fd cognitive runtime + typed broker + root-bound epoch lineage + external repack authority, then test against loop-subrange and split controls.
